formulas.formula: Plan every paycheck, see your bills on a calendar, tick them off, and make the most of your extra paychecks.
Type the year, like 2027. Blank = this year, and the sheet moves on to the new year on Jan 1.
Fills in from the year above (this year if blank).
="Any payday works, even an old one. First payday this year: "&IF(N(D13)=0,"none",TEXT(Paychecks!$B$2,"mmm d, yyyy"))
The month you start budgeting. Earlier months stay empty.
What lands in your bank account each payday.
Money in your account on the 1st of your start month. It carries into paycheck #1.
Counted for you: every 2 weeks from your payday.
Months with 3 paydays. Plan them on the Extra Paychecks tab.

=IF(N(D13)=0,"-",IF('Extra Paychecks'!$C$15="","None",LEFT('Extra Paychecks'!$C$13,3)&IF('Extra Paychecks'!$D$15="","",", "&LEFT('Extra Paychecks'!$D$13,3))&IF('Extra Paychecks'!$E$15="","",", "&LEFT('Extra Paychecks'!$E$13,3))))
To change it, select the money cells and use Format > Number.
1. In YOUR SETUP, type one of your paydays (any one, even an old one) and your usual paycheck.
2. Open Budget Plan. List your bills with the amount, how often they come and the due date.
3. Still on Budget Plan, type how much each paycheck gives to spending (groceries, gas...) and savings.
4. Each bill is paid by the last payday on or before its due date. Bill Schedule shows them all.
5. Open Paychecks: Plan Balance carries what's left from one paycheck into the next. 'Short' means
the money runs out there: save more from the paychecks before it, or lower some spending.
6. Each month tab opens with a calendar of your paydays and bills. Tick each bill when you pay it.
7. Log paychecks, purchases and savings on Transactions. Bills are ticked, not logged.
8. Months with 3 paydays: plan where the extra money goes on Extra Paychecks.
9. Calendar shows any month big and ready to print. Pick the month at the top.
10. Use Savings Goals, Debt Payoff, Subscriptions and Net Worth to see the bigger picture.
11. The example numbers show a whole year. To start fresh: on Transactions select columns A to F from
row 2 down and press Delete. Untick the bills and clear Actual on each month tab, clear the
amounts on Extra Paychecks and Change Pay To on Paychecks, then type over the other examples.
Your year at a glance: totals, charts, top categories and highlights.
Your income, bills, spending and savings, and how often each one comes.
All 26 (or 27) paydays: what each paycheck covers and what's left.
A big monthly calendar of paydays and bills. Pick any month and print it.
Every bill, every month, and the payday that pays it. Green = paid.
Your 3-paycheck months and where the extra money goes.
One list for paychecks, purchases and savings transfers.
A calendar, a bill checklist and each paycheck's Plan vs. Actual.
Every category, every month, with totals and monthly averages.
Goals with progress bars and how many paychecks to go.
Your debts, how much you paid down and months left.
Everything you pay for regularly, and what you'd save by cancelling.
What you own minus what you owe, month by month, with a chart.
White cells: type your numbers here.
Tinted cells: these calculate for you. No typing needed.
Red: something to check (a short paycheck, over plan, a missing category).
Green: paid, payday, on track or better than planned.
Yellow: worth a look (a bill due before your first payday, an amount typed but not ticked).
Two months a year bring a 3rd paycheck. Decide where it goes before it lands.
Bills due right after payday are the easiest to cover. Ask companies to move due dates if a paycheck is short.
Pay yourself first: move savings out on payday, before you spend.
Plan yearly costs (insurance, registration) as a small amount every paycheck.
Buy with a credit card? Log each purchase in its category, and tick the card payment as a bill.
Thank you for your purchase! Here's to calm, planned paydays.
Everything here updates from your Transactions, the bills you tick and your Paychecks.
Tip: Paychecks shows every paycheck's plan and running balance. 'Short' means the money runs out there: save more from the paychecks before it.
Amount: per paycheck for 'Every paycheck', otherwise per bill. Each bill is paid by the last payday on or before its due date. Rename categories, but don't insert or delete rows.
Left to Plan (aim for $0 or a little more)
How Often: Every paycheck (spending, savings), Monthly, Every 3 months, Every 6 months, Yearly or One time. Due Date: type a date like 1/15. For monthly bills only the day counts.
Bills need a due date (they go on the calendar). Red category name: it's listed twice, has amounts but no name, or uses * ? ~, is only a number or starts with < > = (rename it).
Per Paycheck is the average to set aside from each paycheck. The Paychecks tab shows what each paycheck really covers.

Paid every 2 weeks: 26 paydays a year (27 when the first one is Jan 1). A month with 3 paydays has an extra paycheck (★): plan it on the Extra Paychecks tab.
Change Pay To: type a different amount for one paycheck (a bonus, overtime, a smaller check). Leave it blank to use your usual paycheck from Start Here.
Plan Balance: your starting balance plus what's left from every paycheck so far. Short means the plan runs out there: save more from the paychecks before it.
Bills Paid comes from the bills you tick on the month tabs. Bank Balance does the same as Plan Balance with what really happened.
Each paycheck covers its payday through the day before the next one. Paid a day early? Date it on your payday so it lands on the right paycheck.

="The last paycheck covers through Dec 31. Next January's bills due before your first payday then (like rent on the 1st) aren't in this plan: keep "&TEXT($T$8,"$#,##0.00")&" of its Left to Plan for them."

Pick from the list, or type 3 letters like Sep.
★ Payday (green)     ✓ Paid     Tinted days have bills due     Yellow = today

To print: File > Print, pick this tab, Fit to width.

Paid every 2 weeks, you get 26 paychecks a year, not 24, so 2 months (sometimes 3) have 3 paydays.
The 3rd one often pays next month's early bills (like rent on the 1st). Safe to Plan is what you can use without
any later paycheck going short. Extras share that money, so planning more on one leaves less for the next.
Top up your emergency fund · Pay extra on the debt with the highest rate · Get ahead on a yearly bill
(insurance, registration) · Fill a sinking fund (holidays, car repairs) · Keep a small part as a treat.

In a month with 3 paydays the plan counts 3 paychecks of spending and savings, so vs. Plan looks better that month.
Pick a goal from your Savings categories (or type your own), then add the Target and what you had saved when you started (Starting Balance).
Added This Year fills in from Transactions: every transfer you log to that category counts, including money from an extra paycheck.
Per Paycheck comes from Budget Plan. Paychecks to Go = what's left divided by that amount.
Tip: build a starter emergency fund of $1,000 first, then grow it to 3-6 months of expenses.

Pick a debt from your Bills (its payment is a bill on Budget Plan), then type the balance when you started, the interest rate (22.99 or 22.99%) and, once a month, the Current Balance from your statement.
Paid This Year = the payments you tick on the month tabs + any extra payment you log on Transactions (like one from an extra paycheck).
Interest & Charges = what you paid minus how much the balance went down. Monthly Payment comes from Budget Plan; Months Left assumes you keep paying it.
Snowball: pay extra on Payoff Order 1 (the smallest balance) first. When it's gone, roll its payment into the next one.
'Payment too low' means the payment doesn't cover the monthly interest yet. A rate under 1%? Type it with the % sign, like 0.9%.

formula: OR($K2="Payment too low",$K2="Add it to Budget Plan",$K2="Fix a payment")

formulas.formula: Cancel the ones marked Cancel and you save per year:
Billing: pick Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly or Yearly. Monthly and Yearly Cost fill in.
Renews On: the next date you'll be charged. Set a reminder a few days before.
Put the ones you keep on Budget Plan as bills, so they show on your calendar.
Once a month, type what you own (assets) and what you owe (debts). Net worth = assets - debts.
Don't worry if it's negative at first (student loans do that). Watch the line go up.
